title: What is known about 1RB1LD_0LC0RA_1RA1LC_1RE0LC_---1RF_0RD0RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_0LC0RA_1RA1LC_1RE0LC_---1RF_0RD0RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. After step 43,506 the left end of the tape never moves again. The tape is an irregular region of ones-runs separated by single 0s, then a tail (10)^n. Each tick the head zigzags left across the tail and runs back, adding a cell. The two sweeps are proved in Lean. Unlike a counter, the irregular region grows in proportion to the number of ticks, and a tick can rewrite it at any depth. No structure that would decide halting has been found.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: F with 0 under the head, 0 right, 0 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 35,289 cells have been visited and 25,910 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.474).

claims.title: The sweeps across the tail
claims.text: Going left, the head zigzags across (10)^n in states C and A, two cells every four steps (zig). Going right in state B, it runs across in one step a cell, rewriting each 10 as 01 (run_right). Both hold for every n and every tape around.

claims.title: Both parts grow linearly in the ticks
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps the left end is last extended at step 43,506. At steps 2.8·10<sup>6</sup>, 2.5·10<sup>7</sup> and 10<sup>8</sup>, the irregular region has 1,528, 4,060 and 7,904 cells and the tail has 374, 1,006 and 1,931 copies of 10. The tape grows by one cell per tick, so both parts grow like the square root of the time.

claims.title: What the irregular region is made of
claims.text: At step 10<sup>8</sup> the region is a sequence of ones-runs separated by single 0s. Of its 1,191 runs, 679 have length 6, 246 length 2, 193 length 10, and the rest are rare defects (lengths 0, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 14).

claims.title: Rewrites at every depth
claims.text: Over the 11,392 ticks in the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps, about half change only the last 20 cells of the region. The rest reach back with a slowly decaying, heavy-tailed distribution: 563 reach 20–39 cells, 109 reach 80–99, and still 30 reach 720–739. This is not the geometric fall-off of a counter.

claims.title: Why it is hard
claims.text: The machine halts only when D reads 0 with a 0 to its right (E reading 0 is its only undefined transition). The irregular region looks like the output of a process with long-range signals rather than a counter, and no rule for it has been found. It might hide a simpler structure at a larger scale.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 24, history 1 up to width 24, history 2 up to width 24, history 3 up to width 24, LRU history up to width 22 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 20, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..9; n = 10 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The open part is the dynamics of the irregular region.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine builds an irregular sequence of runs of ones, mostly 2, 6 or 10 long, next to a tail of 10s. Each tick the head zigzags across the tail and back. Now and then the sequence is rewritten far from its end. This page runs the real machine in your browser and shows what is known. The sweeps are proved in Lean.

facts.text: Across the tail of 10s, for every length, proved in Lean.
The usual lengths of the runs of ones in the irregular region.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.474).
After 109 steps the tape spans 35,289 cells (48 left of the start, 26,301 right), with a density of 1s of 0.734.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: An irregular region and a tail
html: Watch the head when it turns at the right end. The tape is [irregular region] (10)^n, and the left end has not moved since step 43,506. A tick is a round trip across the tail. The head zigzags left in states C and A, two cells every four steps (zig). Near the tail's left end it turns, sometimes after changing the region, and runs back right in state B (run_right). Each tick adds one cell.
The irregular region is a sequence of runs of ones separated by single 0s. At step 108, of its 1,191 runs, 679 have length 6, 246 length 2 and 193 length 10. Here are its first runs at that moment:

sections.heading: Linear growth, long-range rewrites
html: Both parts grow in proportion to the number of ticks, the region about four times as fast as the tail, measured in cells. So the region is not a counter, which would grow like a logarithm. How far back a tick rewrites it also has a heavy tail: about half of the ticks touch only the last 20 cells, but changes 700 cells back are still common.

sections.heading: What would decide it
html: The machine halts only when D reads 0 with a 0 to its right. Deciding it needs a rule for the irregular region, such as a description of the signals that rewrite it, or a larger-scale structure in the sequence of 2s, 6s and 10s. None has been found yet.

summary: An irregular region of ones-runs (mostly 2, 6 and 10 long) that is rewritten by signals of every range, beside a tail of 10s that the head zigzags across once per tick; both grow linearly in the number of ticks.
family: irregular region beside a growing block
